import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/titanic.csv')

# Create a figure and axes
plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))

# Create a bar plot to visualize survival rate by Pclass and Sex
# This combination often reveals significant insights into Titanic survival patterns.
sns.barplot(data=df, x='pclass', y='survived', hue='sex', palette='viridis', errorbar=None)

# Add title and labels
plt.title('Survival Rate on Titanic by Passenger Class and Sex', fontsize=16)
plt.xlabel('Passenger Class', fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel('Survival Rate', fontsize=12)

# Customize x-axis ticks for better readability
plt.xticks(ticks=[0, 1, 2], labels=['First Class', 'Second Class', 'Third Class'], fontsize=10)
plt.yticks(fontsize=10)

# Add a legend
plt.legend(title='Sex', title_fontsize='12', fontsize='10')

# Add grid for better readability
plt.grid(axis='y', linestyle='--', alpha=0.7)

# Adjust layout to prevent labels from overlapping
plt.tight_layout()

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
